units.notes: Exactly 5 mL for United States nutrition labeling. UCUM encodes it as [tsp_m] and calls it a metric teaspoon, but lists it among US volumes. Distinct from volume.teaspoon.us.culinary, which is the same magnitude as an inexact kitchen rounding rather than a defined quantity.

The 5 mL metric measuring spoon, not an ordinary household utensil. Bare English teaspoon forms are not aliases; metric teaspoon and metric teaspoons are. Another language's teaspoon words select it under a source locale of that language where its recipes conventionally use the 5 mL measuring spoon. A word with competing conventions, such as Portuguese cc and Turkish çay kaşığı, has no alias. A source that states a different measure, such as an equivalent in millilitres, takes precedence. Distinct from volume.teaspoon.us.legal, the same magnitude as an exact United States labeling measure, and volume.teaspoon.au.

The 15 mL metric measuring spoon, not an ordinary household utensil. metric tablespoon and metric tablespoons select it; bare English tablespoon forms do not, because Australian sources use 20 mL (volume.tablespoon.au). Another language's tablespoon words select it under a source locale of that language where its recipes conventionally use the 15 mL measuring spoon. Turkish yemek kaşığı has no alias because Turkish sources give both 10 mL and 15 mL. A labeling convention with a different household tablespoon, such as Brazil's 10 mL, is not this identity. A source that states a different measure, such as an equivalent in millilitres, takes precedence. Distinct from volume.tablespoon.us.legal, the same magnitude as an exact United States labeling measure.

Exactly 15 mL for United States nutrition labeling. UCUM encodes it as [tbs_m] and calls it a metric tablespoon, but lists it among US volumes. It is not the 20 mL Australian tablespoon. Distinct from volume.tablespoon.us.culinary, which is the same magnitude as an inexact kitchen rounding rather than a defined quantity.

The 250 mL cup of ordinary metric culinary practice. volume.cup.au is the separately sourced Australian identity of the same magnitude, and volume.cup.us.legal is the 240 mL cup that UCUM encodes as [cup_m].

Exactly 240 mL for United States nutrition labeling. UCUM encodes it as [cup_m] and calls it a metric cup, but lists it among US volumes; it is not the 250 mL cup that ordinary culinary usage calls a metric cup. Distinct from volume.cup.us.culinary, which is the same magnitude as an inexact kitchen rounding rather than a defined quantity.
The United States dry pint is a different unit and is not registered.
The United States dry quart is a different unit and is not registered.
Approximate kitchen equivalence, not the identity asserted by an unqualified US cup. Use only when the source explicitly defines the 240 mL convention.
Approximate kitchen equivalence, not the identity asserted by an unqualified US tablespoon. Use only when the source explicitly defines the 15 mL convention.
Approximate kitchen equivalence, not the identity asserted by an unqualified US teaspoon. Use only when the source explicitly defines the 5 mL convention.
The 250 mL Australian cup, selected by the en-AU bare forms and by the qualified form Australian cup in any English locale.
The 20 mL Australian tablespoon, selected by the en-AU bare forms and by the qualified form Australian tablespoon in any English locale.
The 200 mL measuring cup of Japanese recipes. It is not the 180 mL rice-cooker cup.
The 200 mL measuring cup of Korean recipes.
The 5 mL Australian teaspoon, selected by the en-AU bare forms and by the qualified form Australian teaspoon in any English locale.
One twentieth of an imperial pint. The US fluid ounce is one sixteenth of a US liquid pint and is a different unit.

A segment of a garlic bulb or a similar bulb. A broad word that also names another segment or piece has no alias on its own: French gousse (also a vanilla pod), Swedish klyfta, Italian spicchio (also a fruit segment), Korean 쪽, and Chinese 瓣. An importer may read such a word as a clove when the ingredient the line names selects that sense, as in gousse d'ail.

A sealed metal can. A broad word that also names other containers has no alias on its own: French boîte (also a box; boîte de conserve is an alias) and Italian scatola. An importer may read such a word as a can when the ingredient the line names selects that sense, as in scatola di pomodori pelati.
